summary.text: A 20-year-old man with longstanding poorly controlled type 1 diabetes was admitted on 28 February 2024 after over one month of cough/sputum/wheezing and outside bronchoscopic pathology consistent with right-lung mucormycosis. He was emaciated with mild dyspnea, abnormal breath sounds, fasting glucose 22.48 mmol/L, albumin 29.2 g/L, CRP 39.9 mg/L and normal WBC 4.60×10⁹/L with neutrophils 75.5%. SARS-CoV-2 PCR was negative and sputum grew ESBL-positive Klebsiella. CT showed bilateral opacities with prominent right-upper-lobe cavities. Meropenem/supportive care and IV amphotericin complex 50→150 mg were started; inadequate glycemic control led from scheduled insulin to pump basal 124 units/24 h with 12 unit preprandial boluses. Day 4 fever resolved and day 7 WBC was 6.38×10⁹/L, neutrophils 62.1%, CRP 9.6 mg/L and serum albumin 34.7 g/L. Nebulized amphotericin was added day 10; day 13 CT improved but cavities remained. In the subsequent step-down phase, whose exact start dates were not specified, meropenem was de-escalated to piperacillin-tazobactam, and IV antifungal was stopped after 10 full-dose days in favor of oral isavuconazole 200 mg daily. Day 16 fever recurred to 39.8°C with suspected PM relapse; family declined high-risk bronchoscopy after counseling. Meropenem was restarted and day 21 combined with IV etimicin after Klebsiella confirmation, with persistent fever/suboptimal response. Family requested discharge day 23 and cefdinir was prescribed for transfer. Death was learned two months into follow-up; exact death date is unknown.

summary.text: A 42-year-old woman with two years of follicular lymphoma on maintenance obinutuzumab was admitted 19 September 2023 after two months of paroxysmal cough/wheezing, recurrent outside admissions and worsening two days after discharge despite moxifloxacin, methylprednisolone and bromhexine. Outside CT showed left pneumonia; admission CT showed right subpleural opacities. Initial vitals included saturation 97%, CRP 84 mg/L, WBC 4.21×10⁹/L and eosinophils 0.03×10⁹/L. COVID PCR was positive and treatment included simnotrelvir/ritonavir, IV cefoperazone-sulbactam and ambroxol. Day 7 PCR became negative but symptoms persisted, prompting bronchoscopy/BAL. Day 9 mNGS detected Klebsiella, Rhizopus delemar(710 reads/high signal), R. oryzae(453 reads/high), Candida and parainfluenza; BAL culture grew Aspergillus flavus. Detection alone does not establish each organism’s causal role. IV piperacillin-tazobactam, voriconazole 0.3 g every 12 h and amphotericin complex 50→250 mg were given for bacterial/Aspergillus/mucormycosis disease. Day 17 tests showed WBC 3.19×10⁹/L, monocytes 15.5%, lymphocytes 0.44×10⁹/L and albumin 36.7 g/L. Sequential oral isavuconazole preceded discharge after 21 days. After two months of continuous therapy, residual right-lower-lobe subpleural CT foci were significantly improved. Day 7 dates the negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR; the following bronchoscopy occurred before Day 9 results, but its exact procedure day and the amphotericin titration/step-down dates are unstated.

summary.text: A 57-year-old man with two years of esophageal and lung squamous cancers treated with multiple radiotherapy/immunotherapy courses and hypothyroidism was admitted after three months of cough/sputum and failed outside oral voriconazole for Aspergillus-positive sputum. He had exertional dyspnea/wheezing, copious mucoid sputum, saturation 93%, neutrophils 93.9%, WBC 7.19×10⁹/L, CRP 19 mg/L and bilateral CT opacities. Initial treatment included meropenem, voriconazole and methylprednisolone 40 mg. Day 4 PFT showed very severe mixed predominantly obstructive dysfunction (FEV1/FVC 46.86%, FEV1pred 33%; post-bronchodilator 51.55%/34%), prompting COPD diagnosis and Breztri inhalation. Day 13 BAL and day 15 mNGS found Klebsiella 2961 reads/strong and Rhizopus arrhizus 101 reads/medium. Suboptimal voriconazole led to IV amphotericin complex 50 mg daily titrated to 250 mg daily, then oral isavuconazole after 10 full-dose days. Day 25 face/neck edema accompanied worsening CT lesions/nodules, small pericardial effusion and extensive left-arm venous thrombosis; pulmonary CTA showed no significant abnormality. Day 27 CRP 57.1 mg/L, BNP 246 pg/mL and D-dimer 1.80 mg/L accompanied progression. Family declined thrombolysis after fatal-bleeding counseling; anticoagulation was intensified without stated agent/dose. Sudden deterioration on days 29 and 34 required successful resuscitation.
